segments.text: THANK YOU. IT WILL COME UP. THERE WE GO. IN TAMPA. IT WAS CREATED RIGHT HERE IN OUR CITY. TODAY, WE WANT TO SHARE WHAT WE HAVE BUILT AND WHERE WE BELIEVE THIS COMPANY CAN GO NEXT. THAT STARTS WITH A MISSION THAT HAS GUIDED OUR WORK FROM THE BEGINNING. OUR WORK IS COLLABORATIVE, INNOVATIVE, ACCESSIBLE, AND PROFESSIONAL. BUT AT THE CENTER OF EVERYTHING WE DO IS TAMPA -- ITS PEOPLE, ITS HISTORY AND ITS FUTURE. WE WANT TO BE PART OF WHAT MAKES TAMPA TAMPA. FOR ME, THAT MISSION IS PERSONAL BECAUSE IT GOES BACK TO WHY I STARTED TEACHING IN TAMPA IN THE FIRST PLACE. MY STORY HERE BEGAN IN 2002 WHEN MY HUSBAND AND I OPENED THE BALLET SCHOOL WITH JUST THREE STUDENTS. FROM THE BEGINNING, I HAVE BELIEVED TALENT EXISTS EVERYWHERE, BUT OPPORTUNITY DOES NOT. OUR STUDENTS WENT ON TO CAREERS WITH COMPANIES INCLUDING AMERICAN BALLET THEATER, HAMBURG BALLET, HOUSTON BALLET, ORLANDO BALLET AND BALLETX. WE KEEP SEEING TALENTED ARTISTS LEAVE TAMPA WHEN THEY WERE READY FOR PROFESSIONAL CAREERS. IN 2018, SIX DANCERS CAME TOGETHER TO CHANGE THAT. AND TAMPA CITY BALLET WAS BORN. THAT NEED FOR PROFESSIONAL OPPORTUNITY IS REALLY WHAT TAMPA CITY BALLET WAS CREATED TO ADDRESS. TODAY, WE CREATE ORIGINAL CONTEMPORARY BALLET WHILE BUILDING PROFESSIONAL OPPORTUNITIES FOR EMERGING ARTISTS. WE WANT ARTISTS TO BE ABLE TO TRAIN HERE, CREATE HERE, PERFORM HERE, AND BUILD A CAREER HERE. WHAT'S BEEN EXCITING IS SEEING HOW TAMPA HAS RESPONDED AS THE COMPANY HAS GROWN. WE NOW PRODUCE MORE THAN 20 PERFORMANCES EACH SEASON, ACROSS MORE THAN 15 VENUES AND COMMUNITY SPACES AND MORE THAN 30% OF OUR PERFORMANCES ARE FREE AND OPEN TO THE PUBLIC. BUT GROWING OUR AUDIENCE IS ONLY PART OF WHAT ACCESS MEANS TO US. THROUGH PROGRAMS LIKE ON YOUR FEET, WE BRING FREE DANCE PROGRAMMING DIRECTLY INTO THE COMMUNITY. WE BELIEVE THE BEST TRAINING SHOULDN'T BE RESERVED ONLY FOR FAMILIES WHO CAN AFFORD IT. TALENT HAS NOT TO DO WITH A FAMILY'S INCOME OR ZIP CODE. WE BELIEVE THAT WE ARE ALSO EXPANDING THAT WORK THROUGH OUR COLLABORATION WITH A PROJECT CULTURAL ARTS PROGRAM TO BRING FREE AFTER-SCHOOL BALLET CLASSES DIRECTLY INTO TITLE ONE SCHOOLS. OUR GOAL IS TO HAVE 300 STUDENTS IN THE HILLSBOROUGH COUNTY PUBLIC SCHOOL SYSTEM ENROLLED IN FREE BALLET CLASSES WITHIN THE NEXT TWO YEARS. IT IS A GREAT EXAMPLE OF WHAT KIND OF ACCESS CAN LEAD TO. ANDERSON IS FROM YBOR CITY AND WAS RECRUITED THROUGH OUR ON YOUR FEET PROGRAM. HE RECEIVED MORE THAN $43,000 IN SCHOLARSHIP SUPPORT. ATTENDED INDIANA UNIVERSITY ON A FULL SCHOLARSHIP. AND TODAY DANCES PROFESSIONALLY WITH BALLETX IN PHILADELPHIA, ONE OF THE TOP BALLET COMPANIES IN THE UNITED STATES. THAT'S WHAT ACCESS CAN DO. WE WANT MORE YOUNG PEOPLE FROM UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES TO HAVE THAT SAME OPPORTUNITY. AND THAT COMMITMENT TO TAMPA GOES BEYOND ACCESS. IT ALSO SHAPES THE WORK WE CREATE. NICOLE IS GOING TO SHARE ONE OF THE BEST EXAMPLES OF THAT. MY NAME IS NICOLE LANCASTER. AS A TAMPA NATIVE, I MIGHT BE A LITTLE BIASED TOWARD THE PRODUCTION I'M ABOUT TO SHARE WITH YOU. AND THAT IS SEPTIMA. THAT'S MAKING SURE THAT WE DON'T LOSE OUR OLD STORIES. PAULA SPENT YEARS RESEARCHING THE PEOPLE AND COMMUNITIES THAT BUILT TAMPA AND YBOR CITY IN THE LATE 1800s TO EARLY 1930s. THROUGH HISTORICAL ARCHIVES, PERSONAL DIARIES, ORAL HISTORIES, PHOTOGRAPH, NEWSPAPER, AND FIRSTHAND ACCOUNTS. THAT RESEARCH BECAME THE FOUNDATION FOR THE STORIES THAT YOU SEE INSIDE OF LA SEPTIMA ONSTAGE. FROM IMMIGRANT FAMILIES, CIGAR WORKERS, LECTORS, SEGREGATION, LABOR MOVEMENTS AND CHARLIE WALL IN THE UNDERWORLD OF EARLY TAMPA. BALLET, LIVE MUSIC, FILM, IMMERSIVE STORY TELLING, WE'RE GIVING PEOPLE A NEW WAY TO EXPERIENCE OUR HISTORY. WHILE LA SEPTIMA LOOKS BACK AT THE HISTORY THAT SHAPED TAMPA, WE'RE ALSO THINKING ABOUT THE ARTISTS THAT SHAPE ITS FUTURE. WE'RE PROUD TO SHARE THAT TAMPA CITY BALLET WILL BE THE ARTIST IN RESIDENCE AT THE UNIVERSITY OF SOUTH FLORIDA FOR THE NEXT THREE YEARS. SO PAULA AND OUR BALLET MASTER, MONTANO, TEACH WITHIN USF DANCE PROGRAM. SIX PROFESSIONAL DANCERS ARE ALUMNI OF USF. 12 ARE WORKING WITH TCB THIS SEASON. THIS CREATES A DIRECT BRIDGE FROM THE UNIVERSITY TRAINING TO PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE. WE ARE ALSO ATTRACTING TALENT FROM ALL OVER THE WORLD. WE CURRENTLY HAVE 200 PROFESSIONAL DANCERS' RESUM S WHO ARE INTERESTED IN WORKING WITH THE TAMPA CITY BALLET. THAT PROFESSIONAL PIPELINE IS JUST ONE OF THE LARGER IMPACT WE BELIEVE A BALLET COMPANY CAN HAVE HERE. IT MEANS ACCESS TO THE ARTS, OPPORTUNITIES FOR TAMPA'S YOUTH, PRESERVING OUR HISTORY THROUGH WORK LIKE LA SEPTIMA, AND ECONOMIC ACTIVITY THAT EXTENDS BEYOND THE THEATER. AS THE COMPANY HAS GROWN, WE'RE BEGINNING TO SEE THE IMPACT ON A LARGER SCALE. WE PRODUCED MORE THAN 220 PERFORMANCES, REACHED MORE THAN 10 MILLION SOCIAL MEDIA VIEWS ANNUALLY AND ENGAGE MORE THAN 50 LOCAL ARTISTS AND CREATIVE PROFESSIONALS PER PRODUCTION WHICH CREATES JOBS. AND A SINGLE TCB PRODUCTION REPRESENTS AN INVESTMENT OF APPROXIMATELY 60 TO 100 THOUSAND DOLLARS. THAT GROWTH IN OUR COMMUNITY AND REACH HAS ALSO BEEN REFLECTED FINANCIALLY. TAMPA CITY BALLET'S REVENUE HAS GROWN SEVEN TIMES SINCE 2018, REACHING MORE THAN $543,000 IN ANNUAL REVENUE IN 2025. THE GROWTH WE'RE TALKING ABOUT IS ALREADY HAPPENING, AND WHEN YOU LOOK AT WHERE THAT REVENUE COMES FROM, YOU'LL GET A CLEAR PICTURE OF HOW THE COMPANY OPERATES. SO MORE THAN HALF OF OUR REVENUE COMES FROM TICKETED PERFORMANCES AND PROGRAMS, BUT WE'RE STILL LARGELY OPERATING BY PROJECTS, WHICH MEANS WE RAISE THE MONEY, WE HIRE THE ARTISTS, WE PRODUCE THE WORK, AND THEN BEGIN AGAIN FOR THE NEXT PRODUCTION. THE NEXT STEP IS GOING TO BE ON THAT CYCLE SO WE CAN PLAN FURTHER AHEAD AND PROVIDE MORE CONSISTENT PROFESSIONAL WORK. PLEASE WORK WITH THE LOCAL BUSINESSES TO MAINTAIN SAFE, RELIABLE ACCESS THROUGHOUT THE PROJECT SO WE CAN CONTINUE SERVING OUR COMMUNITY AND BE THERE ONCE THE PROJECT IS FINISHED. THANK YOU.

THIS ISN'T NECESSARILY THE END OF THE SYSTEM. THE CITY DESCRIBE THIS AS A SPINE FOR FUTURE FLOOD RELIEF. INFRASTRUCTURE THAT OTHER AREAS CAN CONNECT INTO RATHER THAN STARTING FROM SCRATCH LIKE WE ARE NOW. ABOVEGROUND, IMAGINE HOWARD AFTER THE STREETSCAPE IS REBUILT. WIDER SIDEWALKS, LANDSCAPING, BETTER PLACES TO WALK, SHOP, AND EAT. THESE IMPROVEMENTS ARE PART OF THE CITY'S STATED PROJECT PLAN. IMAGINE WHAT FOLLOWS FROM THAT. THE VACANT LOTS AND THE UNDERUSED PROPERTIES THAT WE SEE THERE TODAY DON'T REMAIN THAT WAY. THERE ARE NEW BUSINESSES, NEW INVESTMENTS, AND NEW CUSTOMERS FOR BUSINESSES THAT ALREADY MAKE SOUTH HOWARD SPECIAL. NONE OF THAT MEANS IGNORING THE DISRUPTION REQUIRED TO GET THERE. SIMPLY MEANS WHEN WE PICTURE THE FUTURE, THE CONSTRUCTION SHOULDN'T BE THE LAST PICTURE IN OUR HEAD. WE SPENT YEARS CAREFULLY IMAGINING THE THINGS THAT COULD GO WRONG. BEFORE THIS PROCESS CONCLUDES, I HOPE YOU REMEMBER TO IMAGINE THE BEST CASE SCENARIO. PLEASE VOTE YES.

segments.speaker: ALAN CLENDENIN
segments.text: TYRAE, FOLLOWED BY ROBERT, ASHLEY. NEXT PEOPLE IN THE QUEUE, JARROD DYER AND STEPHEN MICHELINI. MY NAME IS TYRAE VAY, SINGLE MOTHER, SOUTH TAMPA RESIDENT. CARS AROUND ME HAD HAZARD FLASHING LIGHTS ON. AS I CONTINUED DRIVING, I BECAME INCREASINGLY ANXIOUS BECAUSE I DIDN'T KNOW HOW DEEP THE WATER WAS GETTING OR WHETHER MY SUV WOULD MAKE IT THROUGH. MY FIRST THOUGHT WAS TO GET OFF OF BAYSHORE. AS I STARTED LOOKING FOR A RESIDENTIAL STREET I COULD TURN ONTO, I COULD NOT FIND A WAY HOME. THAT'S WHEN I REALIZED THERE REALLY WASN'T A WAY OUT. RESIDENTIAL STREETS LEADING AWAY FROM BAYSHORE WERE DEEPLY FLOODED, TOO. I FELT TRAPPED. THAT EXPERIENCE CHANGED THE WAY I THINK ABOUT STORMWATER INFRASTRUCTURE. THIS ISN'T SIMPLY ABOUT INCONVENIENCE OR HAVING WATER IN THE STREET. IT'S ABOUT WHETHER RESIDENTS CAN SAFELY GET HOME. IT'S ABOUT EMERGENCY ACCESS. IT'S ABOUT PROTECTING OUR NEIGHBORHOODS AND MAKING SURE OUR INFRASTRUCTURE CAN HANDLE THE REALITIES WE'RE FACING AND EXPERIENCING. THE CITY IDENTIFIED FLOODING RELIEF, WATER QUALITY IMPROVEMENTS, UPGRADE UTILITIES, REPAVED ROADS AND REIMAGINED STREET ESCAPE AMONG THE BENEFITS OF THIS PROJECT. SO TODAY I'M ASKING THAT YOU CONTINUE AND INVEST IN SOLUTIONS THAT ADDRESS THE PROBLEMS AND TO SUPPORT PARTNERS WHO CAN HELP DELIVER THEM. I SUPPORT MOVING THE PROJECT FORWARD. PLEASE VOTE YES. SOUTH TAMPA RESIDENTS SHOULDN'T HAVE TO WONDER WHETHER WE'RE GOING TO MAKE IT HOME SAFELY. THANK YOU.

segments.speaker: ALAN CLENDENIN

THIS IS ON THE AGENDA. NEXT, LAST BUT NOT LEAST, YOU KNOW, IF THOSE LINES ARE BROKEN FOR CSX, WHEN STAFF CAME UP HERE OVER AND OVER AND OVER AND OVER AND OVER AND OVER AND OVER AGAIN AND SAID WE HAVE TO GO DOWN HOWARD BECAUSE THAT'S THE PATH OF LEAST RESISTANCE, WAS THAT A LIE? MENTIONED EARLIER SIGNED AND SEALED PLANS, NO THERE'S NOT. THERE ARE NO PLANS FOR THE SHORING. I CAN ABSOLUTELY ASSURE YOU WITH CERTAINTY, 100% CERTAINTY YOU WILL NEED TO SHORE THIS. I'M A PROFESSIONAL ENGINEER, IF I'M MISREPRESENTING THIS INTENTIONALLY, I'M SUBJECT TO CIVIL PENALTIES FOR THIS. I HAVE A VESTED INTEREST IN BEING RIGHT. AT THE VERY MINIMUM, IT WILL COST ANOTHER $25 MILLION TO SHORE THIS PROJECT. PROBABLY MORE ON THE ORDER OF 50. I CAME UP WITH MAYBE 108 MILLION FOR SOMETHING THAT WILL CERTAINLY WORK. ONE OTHER THING I WANTED TO TALK ABOUT, BEEN MENTIONED THAT THERE IS NO OTHER SOLUTION. WELL, THERE ARE OTHER SOLUTIONS AND THEY HAVE BEEN MISREPRESENTED BY THE CITY. HERE IS THE CENTER OF THE FLOODING IN THE NEIGHBORHOOD. YOU PIPE IT OVER. PUT A PUMP HERE. COSTS ABOUT 25 -- THE CITY OF ST. PETERSBURG HAS FOUR ACTIVE PUMPING STATIONS.  TWO MORE ON THE BOOKS. SAY IT COSTS BETWEEN 20 AND 33 MILLION. I HAVE 25 MILLION IN THE BUDGET FOR THAT. $4 MILLION TO RUN THE PIPE FROM THE PUMP STATION TO HOWARD AVENUE. segments.speaker: ALAN CLENDENIN
segments.text: NO, NO. [ SOUNDING GAVEL ] NO CLAPPING. I'LL CALL YOU OUT OF ORDER AND ASK YOU TO LEAVE THE CHAMBERS. HANK, DAVID, CARROLL ANN BENNETT. DR. HANK FISHKIND, FISH KIND CONSULTING. I WAS RETAINED BY THE SOUTH HOWARD BUSINESS ALLIANCE TO CONDUCT AN ECONOMIC ANALYSIS AND COST BENEFIT REVIEW OF THE PROJECT. LET ME SHARE WITH YOU MY FINDINGS. THE FIRST THING I DID WAS TO LOOK AT THE COST BENEFIT ANALYSIS AND ENGINEERING PRELIMINARY DESIGNS. I NOTICED A GLARING OMISSION. THERE WAS NO ANALYSIS OF THE LOSS OF BUSINESS SALES DURING THE CONDUCT OF CONSTRUCTION ALONG SOUTH HOWARD. THE PROFESSIONAL LITERATURE IS VERY EXTENSIVE, VERY CLEAR THAT CONSTRUCTION LIKE THIS HAS SIGNIFICANT CONSTRUCTION EFFECTS AND CAUSES LOSS OF SALES FOR ADJACENT BUSINESSES. I ANALYZED WHAT THIS WOULD COST HERE LOOKING AT EACH BUSINESS. BUSINESS BY BUSINESS, WHAT DID THEY SELL, HOW LONG WOULD THE TRENCH BE IN FRONT OF THEIR BUSINESS, HOW LONG WOULD THE DISRUPTION OCCUR. BASED ON THE PROFESSIONAL LITERATURE AND THE ANALYSIS OF EACH AND EVERY BUSINESS DURING THE 43 MONTHS OF DURATION OF THIS PROJECT, GOING TO LOSE ALMOST A HUNDRED MILLION DOLLARS OF SALES. THAT LOSS OF HUNDRED MILLION DOLLARS OF SALES TRANSLATES INTO ADDITIONAL ECONOMIC IMPACTS. I USE WHAT IS CALLED THE -- INPUT AND OUTPUT MODEL USED PROFESSIONALLY BY THE STATE OF FLORIDA AND ECONOMISTS TO DETERMINE AND TRANSLATE HOW MUCH DOES A LOSS OF SALES OF HUNDRED MILLION DOLLARS MEAN IN TERMS OF EMPLOYMENT AND LOST ECONOMIC OUTPUT. 1100 JOBS ARE LIKELY AT RISK HERE FROM THIS ALONE. FURTHERMORE, THE NEXT STEP WAS TO LOOK AT THE CALENDAR AND TO LOOK AT THE COSTS OF THE PROJECT. AS THE GENTLEMAN BEFORE ME JUST MENTIONED, THE COST OF THE PROJECT IS ESTIMATED NOW AT $100 MILLION. THERE ARE A NUMBER OF ITEMS THAT WERE NOT INCLUDED IN THAT BUDGET, INCLUDING THE BAYSHORE OUTFALL, DEALING WITH CONTAMINATED SITES ALONG THE ROUTE OF THE PROJECT, THE CSX BAYSHORE OUTFALL, SHORING, ET CETERA. THOSE WOULD TAKE THE COSTS FROM A HUNDRED MILLION TO ABOUT 150 MILLION. EACH ONE OF THOSE SIX MISSIONS INCREASED THE LENGTH OF TIME IT TAKES TO BUILD THE THING. IT GOES FROM 43 MONTHS TO 67 MONTHS. THAT'S ADDITIONAL TIME THAT WOULD GENERATE ADDITIONAL LOSS OF SALES. OF OVER 154 MILLION. FINALLY, I PUT IT ALL TOGETHER TO GET THE COST AND THE BENEFITS. ON THE LEFT IS THE CITY'S PLAN. THE COST OF THE CITY'S PLAN IS OVER $300 MILLION. IT'S 150 MILLION FOR THE PROJECT ITSELF. IT'S OVER 150 MILLION OF LOST SALES. THE BENEFITS, IF WE ACCEPT THE CITY'S BENEFITS, THE BENEFITS BEING 118 MILLION. COST BENEFIT ANALYSIS IS .38, MINUS $189 MILLION FOR THE PROJECT AS PLANNED. THANK YOU VERY MUCH.

segments.speaker: ALAN CLENDENIN

AGAIN, KINDERGARTEN CAN BE HARD IF YOU DON'T ATTEND HEAD START. I CREATED A SYSTEM FOR HEAD START FOR BUSINESSES TO BE CONNECTED BECAUSE TAMPA IS GROWING. AND WE WANT OUR BUSINESSES TO BE READY FOR THAT GROWTH, NOT WATCHING IT HAPPEN AROUND THEM. TODAY, I'M ASKING THE CITY TO PARTNER WITH ME FOR BIG FEST 2027 AS WE BEGIN IN TWO VERY SPECIFIC WAYS. FIRST, BY HELPING US CONTINUE DELIVERING WHAT BUSINESSES BY CONNECTING THEM WITH OUR ACCELERATE PROGRAM, DIRECTLY TO CITY DEPARTMENTS, TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, PROCUREMENT OF OPPORTUNITIES, CAPITAL RESOURCES AND DEVELOPMENT PARTNERS. SECOND, TO HELP US WITH THE INFRASTRUCTURE NECESSARY TO CONTINUE BIG FEST. WE NEED HELP WITH COOLING TENTS, SHADING AREAS, HYDRATION STATIONS, WATER, PORTABLE RESTROOMS AND SANITATION. ALL OF THE THINGS ARE NOT AVAILABLE IN THE CITY PARK, RIVER TOWER PARK WHERE I WAS ABLE TO HOST THE FESTIVAL. IT IS VERY IMPORTANT BECAUSE OF THE SAFETY OF OUR COMMUNITY. WE ASKED OUR RESIDENTS TO COME OUT AND SUPPORT BUSINESSES TO BE THERE AND THEY SHOWED UP. BUT UNFORTUNATELY, THE SUPPORT FROM THE CITY WAS NOT THERE. WE'RE LOOKING TO NOT ONLY ACTIVATE IN OUR COMMUNITY BUT ALSO TO ACCELERATE OUR PROGRAMS FOR LONG-TERM COMMUNITY DESTINATION AND HOPEFULLY AN ANCHOR IN SULPHUR SPRINGS. THANK YOU SO MUCH. I APPRECIATE YOU.

SO FAR, OVER 430,000 -- HUNDRED THOUSAND DOLLARS PUT INTO TPD IMMIGRATION ENFORCEMENT TRAINING. NO TAXPAYER DOLLARS SHOULD HAVE BEEN ALLOCATED TO THIS TRAINING TO BEGIN WITH. MORE IMMIGRATION ENFORCEMENT DOES NOT MAKE OUR COMMUNITY SAFER. IN 2025, THE SUPREME COURT RULED THAT I.C.E. CAN RACIALLY PROFILE CITIZENS. TAMPA POLICE DEPARTMENT SHOULD HAVE NO PART IN THIS. IMMIGRATION ENFORCEMENT UNDER TRUMP LED TO A RAPID INCREASE IN DEATHS BY HANDS OF FEDERAL IMMIGRATION ENFORCEMENT WITHIN COMMUNITIES AND WITHIN THEIR INHUMANE DETENTION CENTERS. IMMIGRATION ENFORCEMENT SURGES LIKE THIS LEAVE PEOPLE HIDING OUT IN FEAR IN THEIR OWN COMMUNITIES. PEOPLE MISS WORK, CHILDREN MISS SCHOOL, IT BREAKS MY HEART AND SHOULD BREAK YOUR HEART, TOO. THANK YOU FOR YOUR TIME TODAY.

segments.text: WE CAN, YES. I'M NICOLE, PRESIDENT OF THE NORTH HYDE PARK CIVIC ASSOCIATION. WE SUPPORTED THE 2022 VERSION OF THIS PROJECT, BUT WE CANNOT SUPPORT THIS REVISED PROPOSAL AND WE URGE YOU TO DENY THIS REZONING. WE SUPPORT GROWTH THAT STRENGTHENS OUR CONTEXT SENSITIVE NEIGHBORHOOD BY PRESERVING SHADE TREES, PROVIDING ADEQUATE ON-SITE PARKING AND FUNCTIONAL LOADING BAYS AND RESPECTING THE AREA'S SCALE AND CHARACTER. THE BEAUTIFUL MATURE TREE CANOPY SHOWN HERE ALONG NORTH B IS WHAT WE WANT THROUGHOUT OUR NEIGHBORHOOD AND WE MUST PROTECT THIS NEIGHBORHOOD ASSET. THIS PHOTOGRAPH SHOWS WHY MATURE CANOPY MATTERS. REPLACEMENT TREES CANNOT PROVIDE THE SAME SHADE BENEFITS TODAY. THE PROPOSAL REMOVES ALL 28 TREES, INCLUDING 14 TYPE ONE TREES AND A HEALTHY GRAND OAK. REQUIRE PRESERVING THE GRAND OAK AND MAKE THE GREEN SPACE CENTERPIECE AND MAKE PLANTING REPLACEMENTS ON PRIVATE PROPERTY, NOT ALONG THE KENNEDY SIDEWALK OR IN THE PUBLIC RIGHT-OF-WAY. THE 2022 MASSING COMPARISON SHOWS THAT THE SITE CAN BE REDESIGNED AROUND THE GRAND OAK. DEVELOPER PROFIT SHOULD NOT COME AT THE EXPENSE OF A LASTING NEIGHBORHOOD ASSET. NEARBY PROJECTS SET A STRONG STANDARD. ROME PRESERVED TREES IN THEIR PARKING LOT AND CREATED A NEIGHBORHOOD POCKET PARK. TAMPA GENERAL APPLIED THE KENNEDY OVERLAY WITH 10-FOOT SIDEWALKS AND SHADE TREES ON PRIVATE PROPERTY AND LOCAL TAMPA SHOULD DO THE SAME. FUNCTIONAL LOADING BAYS IMPROVE SAFETY AND KEEP TRAVEL LANES CLEAR. WITHOUT THEM, MOVE-INS, RIDE SHARE PICKUPS AND DELIVERIES USE THE PUBLIC RIGHT-OF-WAY AND CREATE DAILY CONFLICTS. RESTAURANT DELIVERIES NEED CONVENIENT ON-SITE SPACES. WITHOUT THEM, PRIVATE OPERATIONS SPILL INTO THE PUBLIC RIGHT-OF-WAY AS SHOWN HERE AND THE PUBLIC SHOULD NOT BEAR THAT BURDEN. NORTH HYDE PARK ALREADY ACCOMMODATES DENSITY. FIVE OF THE SIX NEARBY EXAMPLES ARE FOUR-STORY APARTMENT BUILDINGS THAT ADD HOUSING WHILE RESPECTING ADJACENT RESIDENTIAL AREAS. THE ONE THAT IS FIVE STORIES IS ADJACENT TO COMMERCIAL AREAS. LOCAL TAMPA BREAKS THAT PATTERN BY PLACING SIX STORIES ASIDE RESIDENTIAL BUILDINGS OF THREE STORIES OR FEWER. REQUIRE A FOUR-STORY STEP-DOWN ON NORTH A.  OUR REQUESTS ARE SPECIFIC AND REASONABLE AS LISTED HERE. THE LOCAL TAMPA DESIGN PRIORITIZES PROFIT OVER NEIGHBORHOOD COMPATIBILITY. THE BUILDING SHOULD RISE ALONG KENNEDY, STEP DOWN TO FOUR STORIES NEAR RESIDENCES, AND PRESERVE THE GRAND OAK AS THE GREENSPACE CENTER PIECE. THIS PROJECT CAN BE IMPROVED. DO NOT CAUSE LASTING HARM AND A DAMAGING PRECEDENT. PLEASE OPPOSE THIS REZ 26-31. THANK YOU.

segments.speaker: ALAN CLENDENIN
segments.text: THANK YOU. IN PERSON PUBLIC SPEAKERS, PLEASE COME TO THE PODIUM. START WITH YOUR NAME, PLEASE. I'M A LICENSED PROFESSIONAL ENGINEER AND TRAFFIC OPERATIONS ENGINEER IN THE STATE OF FLORIDA. I'M HERE BECAUSE THE TRAFFIC IMPACT STUDY FOR THIS DEVELOPMENT WAS BASED ON A 1% GROWTH RATE. THAT NUMBER MATTERS. IT AFFECTS HOW MUCH CONGESTION WE PREDICT. HOW SAFE INTERSECTIONS ARE GOING TO BE AND TRAFFIC IMPROVEMENTS NEEDED WITH THE DEVELOPMENT. CITY PROVIDED THE ENGINEER THE 1% GROWTH RATE BECAUSE TWO TRAFFIC COUNTS TAKING THREE YEARS APART LOOK SIMILAR. I UNDERSTAND WHAT SEEMS REASONABLE BUT I WANT TO EXPLAIN IN SIMPLE TERMS WHY THAT APPROACH DOESN'T TELL THE FULL STORY. TURNING MOVEMENT COUNT IS ONE SNAPSHOT OF ONE DAY. LIKE CHECKING TRAFFIC AT 5 P.M. ON TUESDAY AND EXPECTING THE REST OF THE YEAR TO BE SAME. DOESN'T SHOW LONG-TERM GROWTH, SEASONAL CHANGES. TO UNDERSTAND LONG-TERM GROWTH, WE USE F.D.O.T. AVERAGE ANNUAL DAILY TRAFFIC. SAME DATA USED FOR PLANNING, SAFETY STUDIES AND TRANSPORTATION PROJECTS. IT'S COLLECTED YEAR-ROUND AND ADJUSTED TO REFLECT REAL CONDITIONS. WHEN YOU LOOK AT THE DATA, IT TELLS A DIFFERENT STORY. YOU CAN SEE ON KENNEDY BOULEVARD, TRAFFIC HAS GROWN 3.4 PERCENT EVERY YEAR. ON HOWARD, THE ANNUAL GROWTH RATE IS 5%. THESE ARE NOT ESTIMATES. THESE ARE MEASURED DOCUMENTED NUMBERS COLLECTED BY F.D.O.T. IF WE USE A GROWTH RATE TOO LOW, THE STUDY WILL UNDERESTIMATE FUTURE TRAFFIC. THAT MEANS WE UNDERESTIMATE CONGESTION, SAFETY IMPACTS AND NECESSARY IMPROVEMENTS. I WANT TO SHIFT OVER TO PARKING SINCE IT IS CONNECTED TO THE TRAFFIC GROWTH WE'RE SEEING IN OUR NEIGHBORHOOD. IN 2022, THIS PROJECT WAS REQUIRED TO PROVIDE 452 PARKING SPACES. SINCE THEN, THE DEVELOPER HAS INCREASED THE RESIDENTIAL DENSITY BUT YET REDUCED THE REQUIRED PARKING. EVERY MULTIFAMILY PROJECT I'VE REVIEWED USES SECTION 7, RESIDENTIAL USES FOR PARKING CARD. THAT IS THE SECTION DESIGNED FOR RESIDENTIAL BUILDINGS AND IT IS A SECTION THIS PROJECT USED IN 2022. THIS YEAR, HOWEVER, THE APPLICANT IS USING A DIFFERENT USE, STOREFRONT RESIDENTIAL, WHICH IS USUALLY LISTED UNDER OFFICE SPACES. NO GUEST PARKING, NO MATTER HOW MANY BEDROOMS IN THE UNIT. OFFICE SECTION THEY SELECTED IS INTENDED FOR BUILDINGS WHOSE PRIMARY USE IS OFFICE COMMERCIAL AND SECONDARY USE IS RESIDENTIAL, NOT HIGH-DENSITY RESIDENTIAL BUILDINGS. IN 2022, THE PARKING TABLE MADE SENSE. BEDROOM COUNT, GUEST SPACES AND NEIGHBORS SUPPORTED IT BECAUSE IT WAS TAKING TRAFFIC OFF THE STREETS AND CONGESTION ALREADY EXPERIENCING. UNDER NEW INTERPRETATION, THERE IS NO GUEST PARKING REQUIREMENT. RESIDENT LEASES DO NOT INCLUDE THE PARKING SPACE. THEY ARE NOT GOING TO GET A PARKING SPACE AND FIND SPACES IN THE STREET TO PARK. WE ALREADY HAVE A PROBLEM IN NORTH HYDE PARK AND THIS WILL MAKE IT WORSE. 512 BEDROOMS AND EMPLOYEE AND VISITORS FOR THE RETAIL AND RESTAURANT THEY ARE PLANNING, WE THINK A BETTER PARKING SOLUTION IS NEEDED. MY REQUEST IS TO DENY THIS REZONING, NOT STOPPING DEVELOPMENT BUT ABOUT MAKING SURE WE HAVE THE RIGHT NUMBERS AND COME UP WITH THE RIGHT PLAN. THANK YOU.

I THINK WHAT WE SHOULD DO IS DO A FIVE-MINUTE ROUND AND THEN JUST CALL FOR THE VOTE. FIVE-MINUTE ROUNDS OF QUESTIONS, STATEMENTS, WHATEVER YOU WANT TO DO AND THEN CALL FOR THE VOTE. IS EVERYBODY AMENABLE TO THAT? COUNCILMAN MIRANDA, I SAW YOUR LIGHT FIRST. MIRANDA, MANISCALCO, HURTAK.

segments.speaker: CHARLIE MIRANDA
segments.text: THIS IS VERY DIFFICULT. WHO IS RIGHT AND WHO IS WRONG? CAN'T BE TWO WRONGS AND TWO RIGHTS. WHEN YOU START LOOKING AT SOMETHING LIKE THIS, AND YOU HEAR PART OF THE TESTIMONY THAT I HEARD, WHAT ABOUT FLOODING IN MY AREA. I GOT NEWS FOR ALL OF US. THIS FLOODING IS IN A LOT OF AREAS AND WE HAVE TO START SOMEWHERE. IF WE DON'T START, GUESS WHAT, YOU'RE NEVER GOING TO FINISH. SO WE HAVE AN OPPORTUNITY TO START HERE. I REALIZE WHAT HAPPENED TWO YEARS AGO, YEAR AND A HALF AGO. I REALIZE WHAT'S HAPPENING NOW. THE LAST THREE DAYS, BUT FLOODING IS EVERYWHERE. PART OF IT IS OUR FAULT. ALL OF US, FOR GETTING NATURE AND TAKING ADVANTAGE OF NATURE. THIS IS THE RESULT THAT WE GET, NOT ONLY HERE. LOOK THROUGHOUT THE WHOLE COUNTRY. LOOK THROUGHOUT THE WHOLE WORLD WHAT'S HAPPENING. ALL THE EARTHQUAKES. WE NEVER HAD THAT HAPPEN BEFORE. NEVER HAD THE FLOODING ALL OVER THE COUNTRY. NEVER HAD THE RAINFALL ALL OVER THE COUNTRY IN DIFFERENT STATES. SO HAPPENS THIS IS ONE IN TAMPA. THESE ARE THE THINGS THAT WE'RE LOOKING AT. TODAY, IF I LOOK AT EVERYBODY IN THE AUDIENCE, HAD A WONDERFUL OPINION. I GUARANTEE YOU IF I PUT THOSE WHO WERE FOR TO BE AGAINST AND THOSE AGAINST TO BE FOR, I'D HAVE THE SAME RESULT FOR THE PUBLIC. STAND-STILL, ZERO. NO GO FORWARD AND NO GO BACKWARDS. WE HAVE TO DO SOMETHING SOONER OR LATER. SOONER JUST ARRIVED. THAT'S ALL I'M GOING TO SAY.

segments.speaker: ALAN CLENDENIN
segments.text: THANK YOU, COUNCILMAN MIRANDA. COUNCILMAN MANISCALCO.

segments.speaker: GUIDO MANISCALCO
segments.text: THANK YOU VERY MUCH. I'M LOOKING AT THE TIMELINE HERE OF HOW IT STARTS FROM BAYSHORE AND IT WORKS ITS WAY UP. FROM WHAT I ADDED UP, BY THE DAYS BY PHASE, WE DON'T REACH SWANN FOR ABOUT TWO YEARS OR SO.

segments.speaker: BRAD BAIRD
segments.text: THAT IS CORRECT.

segments.speaker: GUIDO MANISCALCO
segments.text: AT THE SELMON EXPRESSWAY AND HOWARD IS THE LONGEST PERIOD OF CLOSURE WHICH PHASES NINE AND TEN TOGETHER LEAD UP TO LIKE SIX MONTHS. FOUR MONTHS PLUS TWO MONTHS BECAUSE IT'S 130 DAYS PLUS 50 DAYS.  RIGHT AROUND THERE. THAT'S A LONG TIME. HOWEVER, ON MORRISON, MORRISON WILL BE KEPT OPEN DURING THAT TIME. I SEE A NOD FROM KIMMINS. THERE ARE I BELIEVE NO TRUCK SIGNS ON MORRISON. YOU'LL HAVE TO HAVE FOOD DELIVERY AND SOLID WASTE AND EVERYTHING ELSE. IF THERE ARE NO TRUCK SIGNS, WILL THOSE BE TEMPORARILY REMOVED TO ALLOW PASSAGE CONSIDERING THE SITUATION WE HAVE?

segments.speaker: BRAD BAIRD
segments.text: JOHN, DO YOU WANT TO -- SO NO LARGE TRUCKS, I BELIEVE. NO H 20 TRUCKS, IS THAT CORRECT? SO THE DELIVERY TRUCKS COULD COME IN THAT WAY AND THEN KIMMINS' EQUIPMENT WOULD HANDLE THE DELIVERY TO AND FROM THE ESTABLISHMENTS.

segments.speaker: GUIDO MANISCALCO
segments.text: MY QUESTION, AND I ASKED THIS THE OTHER DAY TO SOMEONE ELSE. PALMA CEIA PINES HAS SIGNIFICANT FLOODING. PARKLAND ESTATES HAS SIGNIFICANT FLOODING. WE DON'T GET TO SWANN AND HOWARD AND THEN TO THAT AREA FOR TWO YEARS. IF EVERYTHING GOES TO PLAN ON SCHEDULE AS WE TALKED ABOUT, IF THERE IS A YES VOTE TODAY, WHAT HAPPENS IN THE MEANTIME? IF WE HAVE HEAVY RAINFALL, DOES IT CONTINUE TO FLOOD UNTIL WE GET TO THAT POINT? BECAUSE RIGHT NOW, IT'S A CAPACITY ISSUE, AND WE DON'T HAVE THE DRAINAGE TO ALLEVIATE THAT. SOMEONE SAID THE OTHER DAY, AS WE WORK OUR WAY UP HOWARD, IT WILL ALLEVIATE THE FLOODING. BUT IF THERE'S NO CONNECTION FOR TWO YEARS, IF EVERYTHING GOES ON SCHEDULE, HOW IS ANY OF THE FLOODING -- THEY ARE GOING TO BE FLOODING FOR THE NEXT TWO TO THREE YEARS UNTIL WE GET THERE, OR IS SOMETHING ELSE TAKING PLACE?

segments.speaker: BRAD BAIRD
segments.text: THEY WILL BE FLOODING IN THE NEXT TWO YEARS.

segments.speaker: GUIDO MANISCALCO
segments.text: IT WAS SAID EARLIER, WHEN IT FLOODED I THINK 2015, 2016 AND THEN WITH THE HURRICANES, WHAT CHANGED 11 YEARS AGO, OTHER THAN WE PASSED THE CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT ASSESSMENT AND EVERYTHING IN 2016. WHY DID IT START FLOODING IN 2015? WHAT TRIGGERED THAT? WHEN WE TALKED ABOUT THIS A FEW WEEKS AGO, WHEN I USED TO GO TO SCHOOL THERE AND HANG OUT THERE IN THE '90s, I DON'T REMEMBER ANY OF THAT FLOODING 30 YEARS AGO. COUNCILMAN MIRANDA SAID A LOT HAS CHANGED IN 30 YEARS AND A LOT MORE BUILDING 30 YEARS AGO. BUT IN '15 IS WHEN IT WAS MENTIONED THAT PARKLAND FLOODED SIGNIFICANTLY. IT'S BEEN LIKE THAT EVER SINCE. WHAT CHANGED?

segments.speaker: BRAD BAIRD
segments.text: SO TWO THINGS. STORMS HAVE BECOME MORE INTENSE AND, YES, WE HAVE HAD MORE IMPERVIOUS. WITH THAT, I'LL LET AMANDA ADD. DEVELOPMENT IN GENERAL. ALL THE IMPERVIOUS AREA THAT'S BEEN PUT OUT THERE.

segments.speaker: GUIDO MANISCALCO
segments.text: SOMEBODY MENTIONED EARLIER ABOUT CLEVELAND STREET AND THAT BEING BACKED UP AND THAT PUSHING THE WATER INTO PALMA CEIA PINES WHICH THEN ROLLS SOUTH AND GOES INTO PARKLAND. DOES THAT HAVE ANYTHING TO DO WITH IT? IS IT A LACK OF MAINTENANCE OR OVERTAXED SYSTEM BECAUSE OF ALL THE DEVELOPMENT? I'M TALKING ABOUT CLEVELAND. IT'S ALSO THE SAME ISSUE WITH DEVELOPMENT. IT'S NOW UNDERSIZED. SO THE AMOUNT OF WATER THAT COMES INTO PALMA CEIA PINES CAN'T LEAVE QUICK ENOUGH, SO IT BACKS UP INTO.

segments.speaker: GUIDO MANISCALCO
segments.text: THERE'S NO WAY INSTEAD OF TACKLING THIS AS SOUTH HOWARD PROJECT THAT WE NOT FOCUS ON CLEVELAND? I UNDERSTAND IT WILL PROBABLY BE MUCH LONGER GOING IN THE OTHER DIRECTION, BUT WOULDN'T THAT MAKE SENSE TO ALLEVIATE THAT PRESSURE SO THAT WATER DOESN'T KEEP GOING SOUTH? NOW HAVE TWO OUTFALLS. IT WOULD MAKE IT BETTER.

segments.speaker: GUIDO MANISCALCO
segments.text: I'LL END WITH, WE LOOKED AT OTHER SUCCESS STORIES. I'VE BEEN HERE SINCE THAT STORMWATER VOTE, AND THAT WAS EXCITING, TOO. BUT DALE MABRY AND HENDERSON, AND I DID GO TO CHRIST THE KING MANY YEARS AGO, AND MY DAD HAD HIS BUSINESS RIGHT THERE AT NEPTUNE AND DALE MABRY. I SAW THE FLOODING FOREVER. THAT WAS FIXED. AND I HAVEN'T HEARD OF FLOODING SINCE. YES, THERE WILL BE WATER ON DALE MABRY, BUT WHEN -- AND THIS WAS A KIMMINS PROJECT, I BELIEVE. WHEN THEY SHUT DOWN DALE MABRY AND HENDERSON, IT WAS DONE IN LIKE A 48 HOUR PERIOD, IS THAT CORRECT? IT WAS VERY QUICK TO GET THROUGH THAT INTERSECTION FOR A TOTAL SHUTDOWN. IS THAT RIGHT?

segments.speaker: GUIDO MANISCALCO
segments.text: OKAY. THE THING WITH THAT IS YOU HAVE NORTH, SOUTH, EAST, AND WEST DALE MABRY AND HENDERSON, AND YOU HAVE OTHER ACCESS POINTS. THE DIFFERENCE WITH HOWARD IS, AND THIS WHOLE AREA, YOU HAVE DEAD END STREETS, ONE-WAY STREETS AND THEN YOU HAVE THE CROSSTOWN WHICH CREATES THIS -- WHERE THE EPICUREAN IS AT AND ALL THE AREA, MORRISON IS A CUT-THRU, BUT THE CROSSTOWN THAT DIVIDES IT THAT MAKES IT VERY DIFFICULT, NOT JUST FOR THE BUSINESSES, BUT THEN FOR THE RESIDENTS. I'LL CLOSE WITH THIS. WHY IS IT THAT WE CAN'T DO ANYTHING TO ALLEVIATE THE FLOODING, LIKE AN IMMEDIATE FIX NOW BECAUSE THEY ARE GOING TO BE WAITING FOR YEARS UNTIL THE HOWARD AVENUE PROJECT GETS TO SWANN. THERE'S NOTHING, WE TALKED ABOUT THIS TWO YEARS AGO WITH THE HURRICANES. IT'S NOT A MAINTENANCE ISSUE. IT'S NOT AN AMI POND ISSUE. I'VE HEARD SO MANY THINGS, BUT NOTHING THAT WE CAN DO IMMEDIATELY. BIGGER FIRST TO BE ABLE TO GET THE ALLEVIATION IN PARKLAND AND PALMA CEIA. EITHER DIRECTION YOU GO.

segments.speaker: GUIDO MANISCALCO
segments.text: THANK YOU VERY MUCH.

segments.speaker: LYNN HURTAK
segments.text: THERE'S REALLY NOWHERE FOR THE WATER TO GO. CHAIR IS OUT. I'M CHAIRING, BUT IT'S MY TURN SO I'LL GO. I HAVE A QUESTION FOR MR. ROGERO. BECAUSE WE HEARD QUITE A BIT FROM EAST TAMPA RESIDENTS TODAY. SO I WANTED TO TALK TO YOU ABOUT THE 1.5 MILLION FOR THE BROADWAY AVENUE PROJECT THAT THOSE RESIDENTS REALLY WANT TO MAKE SURE GOES THROUGH. WILL WE STILL HAVE ONE AND A HALF MILLION DOLLARS TO DO THAT PROJECT IF WE DO THIS PROJECT?

segments.speaker: DENNIS ROGERO
segments.text: CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER. GOOD AFTERNOON, COUNCIL. WE INTENDED TO USE ABOUT A MILLION DOLLARS AVAILABLE BALANCE FROM THAT PARTICULAR PROJECT FOR THE SOUTH HOWARD PROJECT. I UNDERSTAND AND I'LL DEFER TO STORMWATER, BUT I UNDERSTAND THAT A WAY HAS BEEN FOUND TO PROCEED WITH THAT PROJECT WITHOUT THIS BALANCE FUNDING WE WERE GOING TO USE. IS THAT ACCURATE?

segments.speaker: LYNN HURTAK
segments.text: THANK YOU. I APPRECIATE THAT QUESTION. THAT WAS MY QUESTION FOR YOU. FOR ME, I HEARD A LOT TODAY ABOUT THE LOSS -- THE COST OF BUSINESS LOSS FOR HOWARD. I COMPLETELY UNDERSTAND THAT, AND I AM CONCERNED ABOUT THAT AS WELL. I APPRECIATE THAT THEY WERE ABLE TO DO AN ECONOMIC IMPACT STUDY. BUT WHAT WE WEREN'T ABLE TO DO IS AN ECONOMIC IMPACT STUDY FOR HOW MUCH HAS BEEN LOST ALREADY FOR THE BUSINESSES ON SWANN, FOR THE HOSPITAL, FOR THOSE PATIENTS, FOR THE RESIDENTS THAT ARE ALREADY HAVE DEALT WITH FLOODING. FOR ME, TO BE ABLE TO USE A NUMBER LIKE THAT, I NEED BOTH. I REALLY BELIEVE THAT THE COST FOR -- SORRY. CHAOS TODAY. THE COST FOR THAT WILL JUST CONTINUE TO RISE. IT'S NOT GOING TO GO ANYWHERE. AND THEN ALSO, NOT ONLY IS IT THE CITY'S JOB TO FIND A SOLUTION TO THIS, I MEAN, THIS IS LITERALLY WHY WE EXIST. THE CITY EXISTS TO SOLVE THE PROBLEMS OF INFRASTRUCTURE FOR NEIGHBORHOODS AND BUSINESSES, BUT REALLY IMPORTANTLY, AND I DON'T KNOW WHY THEY ARE NOT HERE. I'M SURE IT'S POLITICAL, BUT NOT BEING ABLE TO ACCESS A HOSPITAL IS JUST NOT OKAY. ANYTHING WE DO, WE HAVE TO BE ABLE TO ACCESS A HOSPITAL. FOR ME, MY VOTE HASN'T CHANGED AT ALL DURING THIS. I DEFINITELY SUPPORT THIS PROJECT. IT'S NOT PERFECT, BUT IT REALLY HAS TO HAPPEN. WE HAVE NO OTHER OPPORTUNITY. THIS IS WHAT WE DO AS A CITY. THIS IS OUR JOB AS A COUNCIL. ANYBODY ELSE? COUNCILWOMAN YOUNG?

segments.speaker: NAYA YOUNG
segments.text: I'LL JUST SAY I'VE BEEN PRETTY CONSISTENT SINCE, YOU KNOW, WE'VE BEEN TALKING ABOUT THIS PROJECT. I DO HAVE A QUESTION REGARDING THE CSX CROSSING. I DON'T KNOW IF WE SPOKE ABOUT THIS BEFORE, BUT IN THE EVENT THAT THAT IS NOT GRANTED, WHAT HAPPENS?

segments.speaker: BRAD BAIRD
segments.text: IN THE EVENT THAT CSX DOES NOT PERMIT THAT, FIRST, I WOULD SAY THAT THAT IS EXTREMELY UNLIKELY GIVEN WHAT WE'VE RECEIVED SO FAR FROM CSX. THEY HAVE GIVEN US A RESPONSE THAT INDICATES THAT WHAT THEY HAVE SEEN SO FAR -- BY THE WAY, I HAVE NEVER RECEIVED A RESPONSE WITHIN DAYS FROM CSX. USUALLY THEY REQUIRE TO US COMPLETE OUR DESIGN OR AT LEAST GET TO 90% BEFORE WE CAN APPLY FOR A PERMIT. THAT'S JUST HOW THE PERMIT PROCESS WORKS. BUT BASED ON THAT RESPONSE WHERE WE HAVE, I THINK THERE WERE FOUR REQUIREMENTS THAT WE DO, THEY SAID IF WE DO THOSE REQUIREMENTS, WE WILL GET A PERMIT. THAT'S BASICALLY WHAT THAT E-MAIL SAID THAT WAS SENT TO KIMMINS WITHIN THE LAST COUPLE OF DAYS. IF WE DON'T RECEIVE A PERMIT FOR THE 60th MICROTUNNEL, WE STILL HAVE THE FIVE BY TEN BOX, EXISTING BOX, UNDER THE CSX CROSSING TO BE ABLE TO USE. THAT WILL STILL PROVIDE SIGNIFICANT RELIEF TO PALMA CEIA PINES AND TO PARKLAND ESTATES. I MEANT TO SAY THAT IN THE REVERSE ORDER. SO I DON'T KNOW IF AMANDA WANTS TO COVER SOME BENEFIT COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH THAT, BUT IT IS SIGNIFICANT.

segments.speaker: ALAN CLENDENIN
segments.text: HOLD ON ONE SECOND. JUST FOR THE PUBLIC'S INFORMATION, WE STILL HAVE A SECURITY ISSUE, BUT IT'S OUTSIDE OF THE DOUBLE DOORS. WE'RE OKAY IN HERE. BUT I WANT TO LET YOU KNOW THAT TAMPA PD IS CONTROLLING IT OUT THERE. WE'RE ALL FINE, BUT PLEASE DO NOT HEAR UNTIL YOU HEAR FROM ME THAT IT IS SAFE TO LEAVE. VERY GOOD. CONTINUE. IF WE DO NOT GET A CSX PERMIT, WHICH IS HIGHLY UNLIKELY -- I MEAN, THAT WE WILL -- WE WILL GET A PERMIT, BUT IF WE DON'T, THE FIVE BY TEN IS STILL ADEQUATE TO PROVIDE SUFFICIENT RELIEF TO BOTH NEIGHBORHOODS. WITH JUST THE FIVE BY TEN, WE WILL STILL TAKE CARE OF ALL 96 HOMES IN THE FIVE-YEAR, EIGHT-HOUR FLOOD. DURING A HUNDRED-YEAR STORM, WHICH IS JUST BELOW LIKE A HURRICANE MILTON STORM, OUT OF 272 HOMES THAT FLOOD, WE WILL BE RELIEVING 131 OF THOSE WITH THAT. IN A HURRICANE MILTON SITUATION WITH 333 HOMES THAT FLOODED, WE WOULD STILL REMOVE 192 OF THOSE WITH JUST THE FIVE BY TEN BOX AND WITHOUT THE 16-INCH.

segments.speaker: BRAD BAIRD
segments.text: I WOULD ALSO LIKE TO ADD, IF I COULD -- I DIDN'T GO BACK AND COUNT THEM FOR THE LAST 40 TO 50 YEARS, WE'VE HAD 40, AT LEAST 40 TO 50 CSX CROSSINGS. WE HAVE BEEN 100% SUCCESSFUL IN RECEIVING PERMITS FROM CSX. 100%.

segments.speaker: ALAN CLENDENIN
segments.text: THANK YOU. COUNCILMAN CARLSON.

segments.speaker: BILL CARLSON
segments.text: I REALIZE THAT THE STATE ALLOWS FOR THE CCNA PROCESS, BUT CAN I ASK A YES-OR-NO QUESTION. DID WE ACTUALLY DO AN RFP ON THIS HUNDRED MILLION DOLLARS PROJECT OR DID WE JUST USE THE -- DID WE ACTUALLY DO AN RFP ON THE HUNDRED MILLION DOLLARS PROJECT?

segments.speaker: BRAD BAIRD
segments.text: WE FOLLOWED THE CONSULTANT'S COMPETITIVE NEGOTIATIONS ACT PROCESS, WHICH IS A COMPETITIVE PROCESS TO SELECT DESIGN-BUILD TEAMS OR DESIGN TEAMS.

segments.speaker: BILL CARLSON
segments.text: THAT MEANS A REVIEW OF MAYBE THREE OR MORE FIRMS WAS LOOKED AT IN THE BEGINNING BEFORE ANY BUDGET WAS SET TO IT. BUT FOR A HUNDRED MILLION DOLLARS PROJECT, WE DIDN'T HAVE A BID. WE DON'T KNOW WHAT ANYBODY ELSE WOULD HAVE BID. WE KNOW KIMMINS IS A GREAT FIRM, BY THE WAY. I'M NOT CRITICIZING THEM. BUT WE DON'T KNOW HOW MUCH SOMEBODY ELSE WOULD HAVE BID FOR THE HUNDRED MILLION DOLLARS PROJECT, CORRECT? IF WE SAVED 10%, THAT MIGHT HAVE BEEN -- IT'S A CHOICE BY THE ADMINISTRATION. IT'S LEGAL TO USE THE CCNA PROCESS, BUT WE MIGHT HAVE SAVED TAXPAYER MONEY TO USE THAT. ALSO, I'M WORKING WITH LISA BECAUSE MY AIDE IS OUT TODAY. DON'T HOLD ANY SLIDES AGAINST -- IN YOUR MYTHS, ON PAGE 13, I FIND THESE MYTHS REALLY OFFENSIVE. I CAN REFUTE EACH ONE. I THINK IT IS A BAD IDEA FOR THE GOVERNMENT TO CRITICIZE THE PUBLIC. PAGE 13. UNDER THE MYTH AND FACT. ONE OF THE MYTHS SAYS THE FUNDING PLAN WIPES OUT THE FUNDS FOR OTHER PROJECTS. WELL, LAST TIME THE CFO TESTIFIED FROM 2032 TO 2043 OR SOMETHING, IT DOES NOT WIPE OUT THE MONEY. I'VE GOT SOME OTHER EVIDENCE ON THAT IF I HAVE TIME. LISA, COULD YOU SHOW THIS SLIDE? HE THEN SAID, YES, BETWEEN -- NOT THAT SLIDE, THE ONE WITH THE NUMBERS ON IT. THE ONE WITH THE NUMBERS. I WANTED TO SHOW THE MYTH FIRST. IT SAYS THE FUNDING PLAN WIPES OUT THE FUNDS FOR THE OTHER PROJECTS. REALLY IT DOES OVER THE NEXT -- THAT IS THE WRONG SLIDE. WHAT WE FOUND FROM THE CFO LAST TIME IS IT DOES WIPE OUT ALL THE MONEY BETWEEN NOW AND 2032. ANYTHING IN THE C.I.P. OR THIS PROJECT IS GETTING FUNDED AND WE CAN MOVE THINGS OUT OF THE C.I.P., BUT THE REALITY IS WE DON'T HAVE FUNDING FOR OTHER PROJECTS. I THINK IT'S RIDICULOUS TO PUT IN THAT THERE IS A MYTH THAT THE FUNDING PLAN WIPES OUT OTHER PROJECTS WHEN IT DOES FOR THE NEXT FIVE OR SIX YEARS. LET'S BE HONEST WITH THE PUBLIC. THE OTHER THING ON THE MYTHS ON THE SAME PAGE, CSX SERVES MACDILL AIR FORCE BASE. I DON'T KNOW IF I'M ALLOWED TO SAY THIS. I BELIEVE THE LAST REMAINING CLIENT SERVES JET FUEL. I WOULD BE SURPRISED IF THEY DON'T SUPPLY MacDILL. I DON'T KNOW WHO MADE THAT STATEMENT. IF I'M WRONG, SOMEBODY CAN SAY THAT I'M WRONG.

segments.speaker: ALAN CLENDENIN
segments.text: WE DON'T RESPOND FROM THE AUDIENCE. [ SOUNDING GAVEL ] WE'RE JUST TALKING AMONGST OURSELVES.

segments.speaker: BILL CARLSON
segments.text: THE LACK OF MAINTENANCE. WE KNOW LACK OF MAINTENANCE CAUSED FLOODING ALL OVER THE CITY. I'LL SHOW THAT IN A MINUTE. I WAS THE FIRST PERSON TO GO INTO PALMA CEIA PINES JUST AFTER THE -- FIRST PERSON FROM THE CITY TO GO INTO PALMA CEIA PINES AFTER THE FLOODING. I TOURED AROUND WITH TWO OF THE FOLKS IN THE NEIGHBORHOOD. WE SAW THE LACK OF MAINTENANCE EVERYWHERE. SAW DEBRIS EVERYWHERE THAT HAD NOT BEEN CLEANED UP. WE KNOW THAT HAD AN IMPACT. INSTEAD OF TRYING TO PROVE THE PUBLIC WRONG, MAYBE SAY IT HAD A 10% IMPACT OR 20%. SAYING IT DIDN'T HAVE ANY IMPACT IS NOT REALLY FAIR OR ACCURATE. LISA, CAN YOU PUT THE SLIDE BACK UP, THE ONE THAT HAD THE BLUE LINE? NUMBER TWO. I HAD JEAN DUNCAN COMMENT ON THIS A YEAR OR SO AGO. ON THE RIGHT, YOU STILL SEE THE BLUE PALMA CEIA PINES HOUSES WILL STILL FLOOD. THERE'S NOT GOING TO BE STRUCTURAL DAMAGE, BUT IF SOMEBODY HAS ONE INCH OF FLOODING, IT'S STILL GOING TO AFFECT THEM. IT'S ONLY 70% FOR A MILTON-STYLE EVENT, WHICH MEANS 30%, WHICH IS STILL VERY BAD. CAN YOU JUST PUT UP THE LAST SLIDE, PLEASE? THE ONE WITH THE MAP WITH THE DOTS. CAN YOU JUST MOVE IT UP. THIS MAP I GOT FROM STORMWATER ABOUT A YEAR OR TWO AGO. IT'S HARD TO SEE, BUT THE RED ARE THE HOUSES THAT WERE FLOODED BECAUSE OF STORM SURGE, AND THERE WAS A COMMENT FROM SOMEONE WHO SAID THAT THIS NEIGHBORHOOD WAS THE ONLY ONE THAT FLOODED FROM FRESHWATER FLOODING. MAYBE THOUSANDS OF PEOPLE GOT HIT BY STORM SURGE. SHOULD WORK ON A SOLUTION BUT THERE IS NONE. IF YOU SEE ALL THE REST OF THE HOUSES, GO ALL THE WAY UP TO EAST TAMPA AND NEW TAMPA, SIGNIFICANT, ALL THOSE AREAS IN THE MIDDLE, THE PENINSULA ON UP, ALL THAT IS GREEN. YOU SEE THAT THERE ARE HIGH CONCENTRATIONS OF THEM. I'VE SAID BEFORE 20 OR SO PLACES DEPENDING ON THE CONCENTRATION YOU WANT TO CATCH. BUT EVERY ONE OF THOSE DOTS REPRESENTS A FAMILY THAT FLOODED. AND WHAT WE'RE DOING IS WE'RE SAYING ALL OF THOSE FAMILIES EXCEPT THIS ONE AREA HAS NO CHANCE OF GETTING ANY HELP. ALL THOSE HUNDREDS OR THOUSANDS OF FAMILIES HAVE NO CHANCE OF GETTING HELP IN THE NEXT FIVE OR SIX YEARS BECAUSE THE CITY IS OVERPAYING FOR A BAD PROJECT.

segments.speaker: ALAN CLENDENIN
segments.text: THANK YOU, COUNCILMAN CARLSON. COUNCILMAN VIERA. IT HOLD ON A SECOND. LISA, IF YOU GO OUT THIS WAY, HAVE THEM TELL ME WHEN THE SITUATION IS RESOLVED. THANK YOU.

segments.speaker: LUIS VIERA
segments.text: THANK YOU, MR. CHAIRMAN. REALLY QUICK, YES AND NO. DOES THIS PROJECT WIPE OUT FUTURE STORMWATER FUNDING AND REVENUE SOURCES WITHIN THE NEXT FIVE TO SEVEN YEARS, YES OR NO?

segments.speaker: BRAD BAIRD
segments.text: NO. AND DENNIS HAS THE DETAILS. WHAT IS LEFT REMAINING FOR REVENUE OVER THE NEXT 20 YEARS.

segments.speaker: LUIS VIERA
segments.text: THANK YOU. VERY BRIEFLY SO I CAN SPEAK. WE SPOKE LIKE FIVE SECONDS. HAVE AT IT.

segments.speaker: DENNIS ROGERO
segments.text: GOOD AFTERNOON, COUNCIL. DENNIS ROGERO, CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER. AGAIN, IN ORDER TO CLARIFY, I BELIEVE COUNCILMAN CARLSON IS CORRECT IN WHAT HE SAID. I'M LOOKING FOR THE SLIDE RIGHT HERE. GIVE ME A MOMENT.

segments.speaker: ALAN CLENDENIN
segments.text: FYI, WE ARE GOOD TO GO. IF ANYBODY FEELS LIKE THEY ARE BEING HELD CAPTIVE, YOU ARE NO LONGER HELD CAPTIVE. FEEL FREE TO LEAVE.

segments.speaker: DENNIS ROGERO
segments.text: IF I CAN HAVE THE WOLF UP, PLEASE. I BELIEVE THIS FUNDING PLAN, THE WAY WE ENVISION IT AND WHAT'S BEEN PRESENTED TO YOU, I BELIEVE COUNCILMAN CARLSON SAID NO OTHER FUNDING OTHER THAN THE FIVE-YEAR RECOMMENDED C.I.P. THAT'S BEEN SUBMITTED TO CITY COUNCIL FOR FISCAL YEAR 27 TO FISCAL YEAR 31. YOU SEE IT BY YEAR. YOU SEE IT BY PROJECT CATEGORY. TOTALS ABOUT $30 MILLION. THIS PLAN FUNDS THAT. AS COUNCILMAN CARLSON SAID, IT DOES NOT FUND ANYTHING OTHER THAN THAT EXCEPT FOR, AS I'VE SAID, THE DEBT SERVICE WE ARE ALREADY OBLIGATED TO. THIS PLAN ALLOWS $30 MILLION OVER THE NEXT FIVE YEARS FOR STORMWATER.

segments.speaker: LUIS VIERA
segments.text: THANK YOU, MR. CHAIRMAN. I'M LAUGHING. TODAY IS SO WEIRD. THANK YOU GUYS FOR THAT. COUPLE OF ISSUES HERE. I REALLY, REALLY APPRECIATE THE FOLKS THAT CAME, BUT ESPECIALLY TWO GROUPS. NUMBER ONE, THE BUSINESSES. THEY ARE ADVOCATING, WHEN I SAY FOR THEIR INTERESTS, I MEAN THEIR INTERESTS OF RUNNING BUSINESSES AND CREATING JOBS. NOBODY HERE BEGRUDGES THAT. I APPRECIATE THE HOMEOWNERS WHO WERE FLOODED AND CAME HERE AND SPOKE OUT OF THEIR DEEP TRAUMA. I APPRECIATE THAT A GREAT DEAL. I'VE SAID THIS A MILLION TIMES. THERE'S BLACK AND WHITE AND THEN GRAY. A LOT OF GRAY ON THIS ISSUE. FOR ME, THE OVERWHELMING THINGS I SEE LEAD ME TO SUPPORT THIS. THERE HAVE BEEN SOME THINGS SAID IN PUBLIC COMMENT THAT I WANTED TO ADDRESS, JUST COMMENTS THAT KIND OF FLY IN THE FACE OF HOW I SEE IT. SOMEBODY TALKED ABOUT THE FREE MARKET AND FLOODING. NO, NO, NO, NO. NOT APPLICABLE HERE AT ALL. SOMEONE ELSE SAID THEY COULD SELL. NO, NO, NO, NO, THAT'S NOT GOOD. AND THEN THIS IDEA -- AND THIS WASN'T REALLY SAID TODAY. IT WAS SAID LAST TIME, THAT WE SHOULD LOOK AT THIS AS DISTRICT VERSUS DISTRICT. I DON'T DO THAT. I REPRESENTATIVE NEW, NORTH TAMPA. ADVOCATE FOR INTERESTS OF PEOPLE. I REPRESENT A DISTRICT THAT WAS BADLY FLOODED. NORTH TAMPA. I FOUGHT REALLY, REALLY HARD. I WAS THE FIRST ONE TO BRING UP THE ISSUE OF GETTING MILLIONS OF DOLLARS FOR WORKING CLASS, MIDDLE-CLASS, LOWER INCOME FOLKS THAT LOST EVERYTHING, FLOOD ASSISTANCE, GOING WELL ABOVE AND BEYOND WHAT FEMA DID. TAKING CARE OF PUMPS OUT THERE. DOING WHAT WE CAN OUT THERE. FOR ME, I DON'T LOOK AT THIS AS EAST TAMPA VERSUS NORTH TAMPA VERSUS WEST TAMPA, VERSUS SOUTH TAMPA. I DON'T DO THAT. TRY NOT TO BE PAROCHIAL TO THE EXTENT THERE IS A CALL FOR THAT. NOT TODAY, BUT LAST TIME THERE WERE. WITH REGARDS TO ALLEGATIONS THAT WE'LL BE SPENDING ALL OF OUR MONEY ON THIS PROJECT, A PROJECT THAT'S NOT GOING TO WORK. SO WE'RE PRETTY MUCH TELLING THE PUBLIC THAT THE CITY OF TAMPA IS USING ALL OF ITS FLOOD MONEY FOR A PROJECT THAT'S NOT GOING TO WORK. HOW STUPID OF A MUNICIPAL GOVERNMENT ARE WE IF THAT'S TRUE. GOD FORBID, RIGHT. THAT'S WHAT I SAY, GOD FORBID. AGAIN, MY ISSUE WITH THIS IS, I TRY TO COME FROM THE HEART ON THIS. BEFORE MILTON, I WAS MORE OF AN AGNOSTIC ON THIS. I'LL BE HONEST. FORMER AIDE, BRANDON ALONSO ON THIS I DID A COMMUNITY MEETING FOR FLOOD VICTIMS. A LOT OF FOLKS WHO HAD BRIEFLY SPOKEN WITH ME ON THIS ISSUE CAME THERE, DRESSED UP IN T-SHIRTS AND LOOKING LIKE THEY JUST CAME OUT OF NOAH'S ARK. IT WAS LIKE A WEEK LATER AND MY HEART WENT OUT TO THEM. I GOT INVOLVED ON THE ISSUE, MY VOTE ON TAMPA CITY COUNCIL AND THAT'S WHERE I COME ON THIS AT. THERE'S A LOT OF APPEALS THAT HAVE BEEN MADE. IN FACT, SOME OF THE PROJECTS LISTED IN THAT E-MAIL, SOME OF THEM ARE ALREADY MOVING FORWARD AND HAVE CONTRACTS AND DESIGNS AND ALL OF THESE THINGS. SO THAT IS NOT JUST TO PUT THAT OUT THERE, WE HAD THE SULPHUR SPRINGS POOL COMMITTEE, SOME MEMBERS FROM THE NEIGHBORHOOD -- THE SULPHUR SPRINGS ACTION LEAGUE AND ALSO JUST SOME RESIDENTS THAT WERE THERE IN THAT MEETING. ALSO COUNCILWOMAN HURTAK'S AIDE WAS THERE AS WELL. SO WE HAD A LOT OF DISCUSSION. JUST TO PUT THAT OUT INTO THE AIR. ALSO, FOR THE 56th AND BROADWAY PROJECT, I HAD A MEETING WITH OUR MOBILITY DIRECTOR, MR. BRANDON CAMPBELL, ALONG WITH TWO OF OUR EAST TAMPA RESIDENTS TO TALK ABOUT THAT PROJECT SPECIFICALLY. AND THERE'S ACTUALLY, THERE MAY POSSIBLY BE, I'VE BEEN GIVEN THIS INFORMATION, THERE MAY POSSIBLY BE ANOTHER ROUTE THAT CAN BE EXPLORED THAT WILL NOT HAVE TO HINGE ON GETTING THE APPROVAL FROM THE BUSINESS OWNER TO USE THEIR EASEMENT. SO THERE IS ANOTHER OPTION, WHICH IS WHAT I DID ASK THEM TO DO. AND THAT IS WHAT THEY DID. SO THERE IS NO -- THERE IS STILL POSSIBLY A PATH FORWARD. AND MR. BRANDON CAMPBELL DID SAY IF THE OPPORTUNITY PRESENTS ITSELF, THAT WE WOULD -- THAT THE CITY WOULD GO AND COULD PURSUE IT. JUST AN UPDATE FOR THAT. ALSO, JUST TO PUT THIS OUT THERE, I'VE BEEN GETTING A LOT OF FEEDBACK FROM CONSTITUENTS IN THE DISTRICT REGARDING THE EXTENDED TIME FOR HOME REPAIRS FOR -- RESIDENTIAL HOMES. I DON'T KNOW IF YOU ALL HAVE BEEN RECEIVING THAT. MAYBE A CONVERSATION WE HAVE LATER DOWN THE LINE. I KNOW THERE ARE CERTAIN PROCESSES AND THINGS WE HAVE TO GO THROUGH WITH OUR CODE ENFORCEMENT OFFICE. I TALKED TO SUSAN DAILY ABOUT THIS. I WANT TO BRING IT TO COUNCIL'S ATTENTION. IT'S SOMETHING THAT WE'RE GETTING A LOT OF CALLS ABOUT. PEOPLE ARE SAYING WE'VE BEEN CALLING AND CALLING FOR YEARS AND THEY FEEL LIKE THERE'S NOTHING BEING DONE. JUST TO PUT THAT OUT THERE. THAT'S ALL.

segments.speaker: ALAN CLENDENIN
segments.text: IT IS A REPETITIVE ISSUE.

segments.text: THAT IS ALL.

segments.text: REMEMBER, GOD GAVE THE PRETTY ONES MORE FACE. COUNCILMAN MANISCALCO.

segments.text: OKAY. VERY GOOD. SPEAKING OF SWANN PARK, I KNOW THERE'S A LOT OF MISINFORMATION. GOING OUT THERE AND WORKING. THIS HAS BEEN A PROJECT GOING ON FOREVER.
